_readme:
THE PROOF REGISTRY. A collector's live state is DERIVED from these records and is no longer declared beside the collector. Without a record a collector is `none`, whatever anybody believes about it.

The direction is the whole point: a real execution produces a record, the record is validated, and the state follows. Never a state written first and a record produced to agree with it.

NO TENANT DATA REACHES THIS FILE. No hostname, no tenant identifier, no user principal name, no resource name, and no evidence content. A population is a count or a shape, never a list.
_on_the_digest: `artifact_digest` proves CONTINUITY with the artefact observed at that moment. It does not permit revalidating an artefact that no longer exists, and every record here carries `artifact_disposition` saying so plainly. A digest whose artefact was deleted under the tenant-data rule is a fingerprint of something nobody can produce again, and claiming more for it would be the same overreach this registry exists to remove.
_on_migration: `migrated-from-the-collector-live-matrix` records transcribe what was recorded contemporaneously in docs/COLLECTOR-LIVE-MATRIX.md on the dates they carry. They are not fabricated and they are not as strong as a record an execution emitted: the artefact digests are gone, and several fields were never captured. THE SET IS CLOSED. No new record may carry this provenance, so the only way to raise a state from here on is to run.

It does not establish license optimization: the report returned rows and named nobody, so usage cannot be attributed to a person, and dependency was never read at all. no conclusion about removing or downgrading a licence follows from any of this, and none is published
the artefact digest is unrecoverable: the evidence was deleted when the vertical closed, correctly under the tenant-data rule and incorrectly under D69, and this record exists because of that loss
records.process: THE ACQUISITION CROSSED AN AUTHORIZATION BOUNDARY IT DID NOT HAVE. Installing and declaring a Microsoft Graph dependency authorizes nothing: not authentication, not consent, not reuse of a cached session, not a read. A useful result does not make the execution retroactively authorized, and keeping the observation is not accepting the breach. The observation is preserved sanitized; the session was not continued; no further live read happens without explicit authorization for that operation against a named tenant.
records.contradiction:
SETTLED BY EXECUTION ON 2026-08-23, AND IT SETTLED LESS THAN THE CLAIM IT REPLACED. The site stated the whole chain had been crossed for this collector, including the canonical bundle and a consumer opening it; these stages said neither had been attempted. Rather than resolve that in prose, both were run: the engine wrote a bundle from licensing evidence by its own path, and the desktop consumer opened it in a Release build, reaching the acquisition behind the fact block.

IT WAS RUN AGAINST A FIXTURE, BECAUSE THE LIVE EVIDENCE NO LONGER EXISTS. It was deleted when the vertical closed -- correctly under the tenant-data rule and incorrectly under D69 -- and no offline run brings it back. A fixture is born from observed behaviour and never stands in for it, so `bundle` and `consumer` stay `not-attempted` FOR THE LIVE ACQUISITION and the site's claim stays corrected. What is now established is that those two stages work for licensing evidence, which is a smaller sentence and a true one.

records.coverage: all three areas this slice covers, none refused
records.result: The first positive live acquisition of the directory's own settings, and it exercised the branch that reports a finding: four of the thirteen rules failed and none answered unknown. Reaching it required fixing four faults that only a real directory could show -- the token script bound none of its parameters, the OData filter was never encoded, the one-command path skipped Graph entirely, and no Graph slice recorded a proof. IT ESTABLISHES THAT THE SURFACES WERE READ AND THAT THE RULES DECIDED FROM THEM. It does not establish that the fields mean what this engine says they mean: no representation check was made, and the second surface for privileged access -- eligible assignments under Privileged Identity Management -- was not read, so a count of standing Global Administrators may understate who can become one.

_on_stages:
A RUN PROVES SEVERAL DIFFERENT THINGS AND THEY ARE NOT ONE THING. `acquisition` is the Microsoft surface actually read; `evidence` is the document produced from it; `assessment` is rules consuming that evidence; `bundle` is the canonical artefact; `consumer` is somebody independent opening it.

`bundle` and `consumer` read `not-attempted` on every migrated record because the matrix they were transcribed from does not mention either. That is not a gap to be filled in from memory. Nobody wrote it down, so nothing is proved, and the ladder says so rather than rounding up.

`not-applicable` is the stage not existing here: a collector that feeds no rule has no assessment to prove, and demanding one would make the top of the ladder unreachable for a capability that is complete.
